outputs.explanation: Panel A is a schematic of breast anatomy plus a classification table; it is not a plot showing averaged data.
Panel B is a schematic illustrating the study's conceptual aim, not a data plot.
Panel C is a schematic depicting the experimental setup for measuring circadian rhythms, not a data plot.
Panel D shows idealized/illustrative oscillation curves used as a cartoon to explain the analysis workflow, not measured data with averages, so it is classified as schematic rather than a real plot.
Panel E shows a mock illustrative heatmap used to depict the concept of correlation analysis within the workflow schematic, not actual averaged data requiring individual points.
Panel F contains an illustrative example growth curve used to explain the method (exponential growth rate), not real averaged data with replicates to overlay.
Panel G contains illustrative example dose-response curves used to explain the drug-sensitivity workflow, not real averaged data requiring individual points.
Panel H shows illustrative example heatmap/mutation matrix graphics representing the genomic analysis workflow, not real averaged data.

Panel I shows illustrative example scatter plots (PCA cluster and 3D parameter space) used to depict the concept of defining subtypes; scatter plots inherently show individual points and/or are schematic illustrations, so overlay of additional individual data points is not applicable.
